newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH KOLO MEAT FIRM SEEKS 1997 BOURSE LISTING.
newsitem.headline: POLISH KOLO MEAT FIRM SEEKS 1997 BOURSE LISTING.

text.p: Polish meat processing firm Zaklady Miesne w Kole SA (Kolo), majority owned by Sokolowskie Zaklady Miesne SA (Sokolow) , plans to enter the Warsaw bourse next year, Kolo's trade director said on Tuesday.

"We definitely plan to enter the bourse next year, but information on when the public offering and listing will be, and on which market we'll be listed, will not be available before January 15," Henryk Dera told Reuters.
Kolo currently has a share capital of 32 million zlotys divided into 3.2 million shares, 50.8 percent of which is owned by Sokolow, listed on the Warsaw bourse's main market.
Dera said the initial public offering would likely amount to eight million zlotys, with most of the funds to help increase production capacity at Kolo's plant in central Poland.
He said Kolo and Sokolow each had a three-percent market share.
He said Kolo expects to make a net profit of three million zlotys this year on sales of 210 million zlotys and five million zlotys next year on sales of 276.7 million zlotys.

A company controlled by Kolo employees, ~Kolo-Bis Sp zoo~, holds 14.1 percent of Kolo shares with the remaining 35.2 percent belong to the state treasury, which plans to sell to employees and suppliers one million of its 1.25 million shares.
